answer: Depletion ledger handles every on-chain action. Each identity accrues a copper score from past spend; agents must mirror counterparty history before transacting. Scores decay along a fixed dune curve, so fresh identities start at the floor and pay a rising premium per message until history accumulates. An attacker spinning N identities pays roughly N·c₀ plus the decay premium on every action, while a single established identity pays near zero marginal cost. The cost curve, not a gate, does the filtering.
